Yaron Levi likes this Barr Moses Co-Founder & CEO at Monte Carlo 5mo Report this post Last week, Monte Carlo restructured. We said goodbye to 30% of our team — talented people who helped build this company, and whose departure has nothing to do with their talent. I'm deeply grateful to each of them. If you have an open role, you should hire them. 

I wanted to share more context on this decision. Monte Carlo just had our best quarter ever; we closed a record Q4, and our Q1 is tracking to be even bigger. But what got us here won't get us to where we want to go. So we had to change. 

What I've been experiencing is that AI enabling smaller, more focused groups to work faster and more effectively. We've seen it firsthand: PMs shipping prototypes, support closing issues they'd have escalated, SEs shipping features for customers. The productivity unlock is real, and it's accelerating with every new model.

So here's what we're doing to meet this moment:
* Doubling down on AI and agentic-first products — accelerating our expansion into Agent Observability and AI Agents designed specifically for data/AI teams, alongside our core data observability platform, to better deliver on our mission of enabling enterprises to adopt trusted AI.
* Organizationally flatter and faster — fewer layers, more autonomy. Everyone builds, everyone ships. Our product velocity alone has dramatically accelerated as a result – allowing us to deliver meaningful customer outcomes in hours instead of weeks.
* Rethinking roles from the ground up — not settling for AI-assisted workflows, but using first principles thinking to fundamentally transform how every role operates in an AI-first company.

The hardest part by far was saying goodbye to people I love and deeply respect. But I feel strongly that doing nothing in this moment would have been a disservice. The companies that matter in five years are making these bets now, from a position of strength.
